item.title: Can we stop antibiotic resistance from ruining promising drugs before they reach patients?
item.description: [Science & Research] Keyword: microbiology — What if we could predict early in drug development which antibiotics bacteria are most likely to become resistant to? In a review published in Nature Reviews Microbiology, researchers from the HUN-REN Biological Research Centre, Szeged (HUN-REN BRC Szeged) and the Hungarian Centre of Excellence for Molecular Medicine (HCEMM) in Szeged propose a five-step decision-making framework that could help identify resistance risks early, refine promising drug candidates and prevent costly failures.

item.title: Summer 2026 heat toll exceeded 50,000 deaths in European cities, analysis estimates
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — More than 50,000 heat-related deaths are estimated to have occurred in urban areas across Europe during summer 2026, with around two-thirds attributed to human-induced climate change, according to new research led by the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) and Imperial College London.

item.title: Marine heat waves suppress nutrient use, reproductive flexibility in humpback whales
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — A new study led by University of Hawai'i (UH) at Mānoa researchers reveals how extreme ocean warming disrupts whale metabolism, nutrition and reproductive success and what the developing 2026–2027 El Niño could mean next. As climate change drives increasingly intense marine heat waves, scientists are uncovering how these extreme warming events disrupt the biology of humpback whales.

item.title: As flood risk rises, some communities question the idea of resilience
item.description: [Climate & Environment] Keyword: climate change — Climate change is increasing flood risk across the U.K. As floods become more frequent and intense, communities are increasingly encouraged to become resilient and "live with water." Yet in some flood-prone areas, residents are rejecting these calls, concerned that resilience is less about helping communities and more about transferring responsibility from institutions to citizens.

item.title: Rare fossils reveal what ancient Denisovans may have looked like
item.description: [Open Source Software] Keyword: FOSS — Whenever anything is written about the Denisovans, the word "mysterious" is almost guaranteed to appear. That is because we just don't know a lot about this extinct human group that may have lived in East Asia from at least 300,000 to 45,000 years ago and was closely related to the Neanderthals. The main reason for that is a sparse fossil record.
